scope: Proposition 3.16 (Affine extremal configurations) of the manuscript “Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation” (preprints/Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-dimensional-wave-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 079 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 79299093c07ea305), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 28-29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: If at least one relevant minimal cost is positive, one can pass to extremizing documented configurations with u(i) = J(1 − i), J ≥ 0, ( b2(i) = q(i − 1), c > 0, b1(i) = c1(i − 1), c = 0 < c1. (F) For c ̸= 1, q = c. For c = 1, either q = 1 or q < 1; no nonnegative lower bound on q is assumed. In the latter option, |β1(T1)| ≤ s−1−o(1) , s|Kl| ≤ s−o(1) at every gate l. For 0 < c ≤ 1 and q = c, one has ℓl|Kl| ≤ sb2(l)−o(1), and the own-time values βi(Ti), βl(Tl) on forward connections differ by at most sb2(i)−o(1). For c > 1, compare instead βi(Ti), Ki 28 with βl(Ti), Kl at respective precisions sb2(i)−o(1), sb2(i)−i−o(1). The linear alternative retains its individual curvature bounds and the center-derivative comparison at precision sb1(i)−o(1). All relevant terminal minimal costs, gate counts, read-mass bounds, Equations (M) and (A), and the permission to insert ordinary regularization persist. Base support, significant normal support, and reachable shear parameters are bounded by fixed powers in every normalized inner experiment.
